Obedience

/oh-BEE-dee-ents/ � second syllable rhymes with bee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Obedience is the act of following rules, instructions, or the wishes of an authority.

The guide dog's perfect obedience kept its owner safe in traffic.

Worked Example

The military recruit immediately stood at attention and executed every command precisely as given, demonstrating perfect obedience to the sergeant's orders.

Obedience specifically means following orders willingly, especially out of respect for authority. Simply saying 'followed orders' misses the element of respect for an authority figure's right to command.

How Obedience Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

compliance

compliance: going along with rules or requests

submission

submission: yielding completely to another's power

discipline

discipline: trained self-control that follows rules

Antonyms

defiance

defiance: openly refusing to obey authority

rebellion

rebellion: active resistance against rules or authority

How Strong Is It? — resistance → compliance → devotion → obedience

resistance vs. obedience

resistance vs. obedience: Resistance sits at the opposite end of the scale from obedience: resistance means pushing back against commands, while obedience means following them.

compliance vs. obedience

compliance vs. obedience: Compliance is a weaker form of obedience: compliance means going along with a rule, perhaps reluctantly, while obedience means consistently following an authority's commands.

devotion vs. obedience

devotion vs. obedience: Devotion goes a step beyond obedience: an obedient follower does what is asked, but a devoted one commits their whole heart, serving loyally even without being told.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ob-

Prefix — ob-: to, toward (Latin)

Root — edi (from audire)

Root — edi (from audire): to listen, hear (Latin)

Suffix — -ence

Suffix — -ence: state or quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Ob- ('to, toward') + the root of audire ('to listen') + -ence ('state of') literally means 'the state of listening to someone' — obedience is listening to an authority and doing what they say.

Use the root in a new word: audible

Use the root in a new word: audible: The whisper was barely audible — 'able to be heard' — from the same Latin root audire ('to hear') hidden inside obedience, which began as 'listening to' commands.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / neutral

Obedience is the right word when describing willingness to follow rules or orders, especially in hierarchical contexts like schools, the military, or families. For mere compliance with rules, use 'compliance'; for the training that produces obedience, use 'discipline'.
